Water softeners for Pinckney and Livingston County homes

Hard water leaves scale in your pipes, water heater and dishwasher, and makes soap work harder. Dan tests your water first, then sizes and programs a softener for your home, whether you’re on a private well or city water.

Signs you have hard water

Hard water carries extra calcium and magnesium. It’s generally safe to drink, but it’s hard on your home.

  • White crust on faucets and showerheads
  • Spots on glasses and dishes
  • Soap and shampoo that won’t lather, so you use more
  • Dry skin, dull hair and stiff, dingy laundry
  • Scale that shortens the life of water heaters, washers and dishwashers

How a softener works

A softener tank is filled with resin beads. As water passes through, the beads hold on to the calcium and magnesium and swap them for sodium or potassium. Every so often the system cleans itself by rinsing the beads with salt water from the brine tank, then goes back to softening.

Single-tank or twin-tank

A single-tank softener regenerates on a schedule, usually overnight while nobody’s using water. A twin-tank softener runs two tanks from one valve, so one tank is always in service while the other regenerates. That means soft water around the clock, which suits bigger households and very hard water.

We also offer refurbished softeners when budget matters. Whichever you choose, it’s set up for your water test results rather than a factory default.

Iron in your water too?

A softener can handle a little iron. When there’s more, or a rotten-egg smell, an iron and sulfur filter goes in ahead of the softener so the softener can do its job. Most of the well-water systems we install are an iron filter and a softener together.

Salt, service and repairs

  • Salt delivery, carried to your brine tank
  • Resin cleaning, salt level checks and performance checks
  • Repairs on most brands, including systems we didn’t install

Not sure if your softener is worth fixing? Text a picture of it to Dan at 734-878-2572. He can come out and evaluate the unit to see if it’s repairable or not. Depending on the issue, sometimes all it needs is a little cleaning.

Common questions

How long does a softener install take?

It depends on your plumbing and the system, but most installs are done the same day with only a short water shutoff.

Can I install a softener myself?

You can, but sizing and programming the valve for your water’s hardness and iron is where most DIY systems fall short. A professional install also keeps product and workmanship warranties intact.

How often does a softener need maintenance?

Keep the brine tank stocked with salt (we can deliver it), and have the system checked periodically. We clean resin, check salt levels, and confirm it’s regenerating correctly.

Do you repair softeners you didn’t install?

Yes. We work on most brands. You can text a picture to Dan at 734-878-2572 and he can come out and evaluate the unit to see if it’s repairable or not.
